Nazi Germany. The totalitarian state established by Adolf Hitler and the National Socialist, or Nazi, party, ruling from nineteen thirty-three to nineteen forty-five and seeking to create a racially pure Aryan empire through militarism, genocide, and territorial conquest. Emerging from the chaos and resentment of the Weimar Republic, the Nazis exploited economic depression, humiliation from World War One, and popular yearning for national renewal to seize power. The regime implemented the most systematic genocide in history—the Holocaust, which murdered six million Jews along with millions of others deemed undesirable—while aggressively expanding eastward. Nazi Germany's invasion of Poland in nineteen thirty-nine triggered World War Two, the deadliest conflict in human history, ending only with the regime's military defeat and the deaths of over seventy million people worldwide.

Hitler and the Nazi party exploited the Weimar Republic's economic crisis, military humiliation, and political instability, appealing to German nationalism, antisemitism, and resentment of the Treaty of Versailles. The Nazis won elections in nineteen thirty-three with thirty-seven percent of the vote, and Hitler was appointed Chancellor. He rapidly consolidated power through the Enabling Act of March nineteen thirty-three, which granted him dictatorial authority. The regime immediately suppressed opposition, using the Reichstag Fire in February nineteen thirty-three to justify the arrest of communist and socialist rivals, establishing a one-party totalitarian state.

Nazi ideology centered on Lebensraum—the doctrine that Aryans required Eastern European territory for expansion—and racial antisemitism, claiming Jews and other groups were enemies of the German race. The regime created a total surveillance state with the Gestapo secret police, SS paramilitaries, and a culture of denunciation that made resistance nearly impossible. The Nazis enacted the Nuremberg Laws in nineteen thirty-five, stripping Jews of citizenship and rights, beginning decades of persecution culminating in systematic genocide.

Hitler withdrew Germany from the League of Nations and began massive rearmament, openly building planes, tanks, and warships in violation of the Treaty of Versailles while Western powers largely acquiesced. The regime pursued a policy of appeasement by Britain and France, remilitarizing the Rhineland in nineteen thirty-six, annexing Austria in nineteen thirty-eight, and seizing Czechoslovakia between nineteen thirty-eight and nineteen thirty-nine without military opposition. The Nazi-Soviet Pact in August nineteen thirty-nine, a non-aggression treaty with the Soviet Union, secured Germany's eastern border and freed Hitler to invade Poland in September nineteen thirty-nine, triggering World War Two.

Germany's Blitzkrieg tactics—coordinated air, armor, and infantry assault—conquered France in nineteen forty, establishing Nazi military superiority. The regime invaded the Soviet Union in June nineteen forty-one in Operation Barbarossa, breaking the Nazi-Soviet Pact and embarking on a two-front war that would ultimately exhaust Germany's resources. By nineteen forty-two to nineteen forty-three, the momentum shifted. The Allies defeated Germany at Stalingrad, Midway, and El Alamein, and the Nazis faced eventual encirclement.

The regime systematized the murder of six million Jews through concentration camps and extermination camps like Auschwitz-Birkenau, along with millions of Slavs, Roma, disabled people, political prisoners, and others. The Final Solution, Nazi leadership's plan to exterminate all European Jews, represented history's most methodical genocide, using industrial technology, bureaucratic precision, and pseudoscientific racism. Slave labor, medical experimentation, and starvation killed millions. The Holocaust stands as the defining atrocity of the twentieth century and a turning point in human conscience.

Germany faced invasion from east by the Soviets and west by the Allies in nineteen forty-four to nineteen forty-five. Hitler committed suicide in his bunker as Soviet forces closed in, and Germany surrendered unconditionally in May nineteen forty-five. The war left Europe in ruins, with over seventy million dead, the Holocaust exposed, and Germany divided and occupied by the Allied powers.
